div.head: V Atr 32.3
div.ab: Ðridde is æt swigean, þæt man wolde sweogian ⁊ on æftergængan eft siððan sprecan, þæt man on forgængan næfre becliopode,
Ðridde is æt swigean, þæt man wolde sweogian ⁊ on æftergængan eft siððan sprecan, þæt man on forgængan næfre becliopode,
Ðridde is æt swigean, þæt man wolde sweogian ⁊ on æftergængan eft siððan sprecan þæt man on forgængan næfre becliopode.
Ðridde is æt swigean, þæt man wolde sweogian and on æftergængan eft siððan sprecan, þæt man on forgængan næfre becliopode.
Das dritte betrifft Schweigen: dass man [Klagen] zu verschweigen pflegte und nachher gegen Nachfolger das einzuklagen, was man niemals gegen den Vorgänger eingeklagt hatte.
The third concerns silence: that people would keep silent [about claims] and afterwards sue successors for what they had never sued the predecessor for.
Thirdly, with regard to the practice of bringing forward, after long silence, claims against an heir which had never been made against his predecessor.
The third concerns silence, that a man would remain silent, and afterwards claim from a successor what had never been claimed from his predecessor.
Thirdly, concerning the bringing of lawsuits against an heir after remaining silent that were never brought against his predecessor.
div.note: Only in D. Liebermann compares III Atr 14.; AU: corrected against Rabin p. 156 / 157, October 2026 (was “Đridde”, now “Ðridde”)

‘sich verschweigen’ im Dt. Recht: Wichtiges gerichtlich nicht sprechen
‘sich verschweigen’ in German law: not raising important matters in court
Toller attests a special meaning in the law of inheritance
